_what:
Every MCP tool, and whether it was REVIEWED for the credentials rule: a tool that needs credentials pre-flights and returns a structured `needsAuth` handoff rather than erroring, so the agent can drive sign-in and retry.

WHY A LEDGER RATHER THAN A CHECK OVER THE CODE. There is no marker that says a tool touches credentials. Compliance is reached three ways — runGuards, a bespoke pre-flight, or nothing because none is needed — and no scan separates them. The readOnly field solved the same problem by making the AUTHOR declare it; this does the same with a row instead of a type, because only 48 of the 114 tools have a descriptor to put a field on.

WHAT THE CHECK BUYS TODAY: a NEW tool has no row, so the build fails and the question gets asked at authoring time. That is stopping the bleeding. Draining the pool is the `unreviewedCeiling`, which may only fall.

A verdict is one of: NEEDS-AUTH (and how it hands off) / NO-AUTH (why not) / UNREVIEWED. Replace UNREVIEWED with a real verdict and a reason; never delete a row for a tool that still exists.
